title: H002: Add multi-stage Dockerfile for deployment
description:
**Size:** 🔧 small
**Category:** infrastructure
**Priority:** high
**Source:** Proposed for 'Perform a GAP analysis. The README.md as well as'

Create deploy/docker/Dockerfile with a standard multi-stage Go build: Stage 1 uses golang:1.22-alpine (or current Go version) as builder with module cache optimization and CGO_DISABLED=1 static build. Stage 2 uses gcr.io/distroless/static or alpine:3.19 as minimal runtime, copies the plexd binary, sets appropriate user/group, exposes relevant ports, and defines the entrypoint. Include a .dockerignore file to exclude .git, docs, and test files from the build context.

**Rationale:** The README documents docker pull instructions but no Dockerfile exists in the repository. Users and CI/CD pipelines cannot build container images. This is a ship-blocking gap between documentation and deliverables.

**Affected Areas:**
- deploy/docker/Dockerfile
- deploy/docker/.dockerignore

stories.title: Developer can build a container image from source
stories.want: to run `docker build` against the repository and produce a working plexd container image
stories.so_that: I can test, deploy, and iterate on plexd without depending on pre-built images from the registry
criteria: Running `docker build -f deploy/docker/Dockerfile .` from the repo root produces a tagged image
The resulting image contains a statically linked plexd binary at /usr/local/bin/plexd
The image size is under 30MB (distroless/static base)
The build completes successfully for both amd64 and arm64 targets

stories.title: CI pipeline can build and push container images
stories.want: a Dockerfile that supports build arguments for version, commit, and date metadata
stories.so_that: automated builds inject correct version info and produce traceable release artifacts
criteria: Build args VERSION, COMMIT, and DATE are passed through to Go ldflags
The resulting binary reports correct version info when running `plexd --version`
Module dependencies are cached in a separate layer to speed up rebuilds
The .dockerignore excludes .git, docs, and test files to minimize build context

stories.title: Security team can verify the container runs as non-root
stories.want: the container image to run as a non-root user with minimal filesystem access
stories.so_that: container breakout risk is minimized and the image passes security scanning
criteria: The container runs as a non-root user (UID 65534 / nobody)
The base image is gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12 with no shell or package manager
The binary is statically compiled with CGO_DISABLED=1 (no libc dependency)
Required data directories (/var/lib/plexd, /var/run/plexd, /etc/plexd) are created with correct ownership

stories.title: Operator can verify the container exposes correct ports
stories.want: the Dockerfile to document exposed ports matching the daemonset and README
stories.so_that: port mappings are self-documenting and consistent with Kubernetes manifests
criteria: Port 9100/tcp is exposed (HTTP health checks and node API)
Port 51820/udp is exposed (WireGuard mesh traffic)
Exposed ports match the daemonset.yaml liveness/readiness probe configuration
The entrypoint is set to the plexd binary without hardcoded subcommands

stories.title: Developer does not accidentally include unnecessary files in build context
stories.want: a .dockerignore file that excludes non-essential files from the Docker build context
stories.so_that: build context is small, builds are fast, and no sensitive files leak into images
criteria: The .git directory is excluded from the build context
The docs/ directory is excluded from the build context
Test files (*_test.go) and test scripts are excluded from the build context
The .dockerignore file lives at deploy/docker/.dockerignore (or repo root as needed)

stories.title: Dockerfile build is validated in CI
stories.want: the Dockerfile to be linted and the image build tested automatically
stories.so_that: Dockerfile regressions are caught before merge
criteria: A hadolint check validates Dockerfile best practices
A docker build --check or equivalent validates the Dockerfile syntax
The test validates that the built image runs and responds to --version
The test validates the image runs as non-root

requirements.description: The Dockerfile SHALL use a multi-stage build with golang:1.24-alpine as the builder stage and gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12 as the runtime stage
requirements.rationale: Multi-stage builds produce minimal images. golang:1.24-alpine matches the project's Go version. Distroless eliminates shell access and reduces attack surface.

scenarios.name: Builder stage compiles a static binary
scenarios.when: the builder stage runs `go build` with CGO_ENABLED=0
scenarios.then: the output is a statically linked ELF binary with no dynamic library dependencies
and_then: the binary can run on the distroless base without libc

scenarios.name: Runtime stage contains only the binary and directories
scenarios.then: the image contains only the plexd binary, CA certificates, and required directories
and_then: no Go toolchain, source code, or build artifacts are present in the final image

scenarios.name: Go version mismatch is caught
scenarios.when: go.mod specifies a different Go version than the Dockerfile builder base
scenarios.then: the build may produce warnings or fail on incompatible syntax
and_then: a comment in the Dockerfile documents the Go version and links to go.mod

requirements.description: The builder stage SHALL optimize Docker layer caching by copying and downloading Go modules before copying source code
requirements.rationale: Module cache optimization means that changing source code does not invalidate the module download layer, significantly speeding up rebuilds.

scenarios.name: Module cache hit on source-only change
scenarios.when: only .go source files change (go.mod and go.sum unchanged)
scenarios.then: Docker reuses the cached module download layer
and_then: rebuild time is reduced to only the compile step

scenarios.name: Full rebuild on dependency change
scenarios.then: Docker invalidates the module cache and re-downloads dependencies
and_then: the build still completes successfully

scenarios.name: COPY order is correct
scenarios.then: go.mod and go.sum are copied before the full source tree
and_then: go mod download runs before COPY . .

requirements.description: The Dockerfile SHALL produce a static binary with CGO_ENABLED=0 and inject version metadata via ldflags build arguments
requirements.rationale: Static compilation ensures the binary runs on distroless. Build args for version/commit/date match the existing main.go ldflags pattern.

scenarios.name: Default build without args uses dev values
scenarios.when: docker build is run without --build-arg flags
scenarios.then: the binary is built with default ldflags (version=dev, commit=none, date=unknown)
and_then: the binary runs correctly with dev version info

scenarios.name: CI build injects release metadata
scenarios.when: docker build is run with --build-arg VERSION=1.0.0 --build-arg COMMIT=abc123 --build-arg DATE=2026-01-01
scenarios.then: the binary reports version=1.0.0, commit=abc123, date=2026-01-01
and_then: ldflags target the correct package path: main.version, main.commit, main.date

scenarios.name: Binary is fully static
scenarios.when: the built binary is inspected with `file` or `ldd`
scenarios.then: it is reported as a statically linked executable
and_then: no dynamic libraries are required at runtime

requirements.description: The runtime stage SHALL run as a non-root user with UID 65534 (nobody) and create required data directories with correct ownership
requirements.rationale: Running as non-root is a container security best practice. The directories match the volume mounts defined in the Kubernetes daemonset.

scenarios.name: Container process runs as non-root
scenarios.when: the container is started without --user override
scenarios.then: the process runs as UID 65534 (nobody)
and_then: the process cannot write to system directories

scenarios.name: Data directories exist with correct ownership
scenarios.then: directories /var/lib/plexd, /var/run/plexd, and /etc/plexd exist
and_then: the directories are owned by the non-root user

scenarios.name: Container can be overridden to run as root for privileged deployments
scenarios.when: the container is started with --user root or in a privileged Kubernetes pod
scenarios.then: the binary still functions correctly
and_then: NET_ADMIN capability can be granted at the pod level as shown in daemonset.yaml

requirements.description: The Dockerfile SHALL expose ports 9100/tcp (HTTP health/API) and 51820/udp (WireGuard mesh) to document the network interface
requirements.rationale: EXPOSE documents which ports the container listens on. These match the daemonset probes (9100) and WireGuard config (51820).

scenarios.name: Health check port is documented
scenarios.then: EXPOSE 9100 is present
and_then: matches daemonset.yaml livenessProbe and readinessProbe port

scenarios.name: WireGuard port is documented
scenarios.then: EXPOSE 51820/udp is present
and_then: matches the default wireguard.listen_port in README configuration

scenarios.name: Entrypoint is the binary without hardcoded subcommand
scenarios.then: the entrypoint is ['/usr/local/bin/plexd']
and_then: users can pass any subcommand: up, join, status, etc.

requirements.description: A .dockerignore file SHALL exclude .git, docs, test files, and other non-essential files from the build context
requirements.rationale: Minimizing build context speeds up builds and prevents sensitive or unnecessary files from being available during the build.

scenarios.name: Git history excluded
scenarios.then: the .git directory is not sent to the build daemon
and_then: build context size is significantly reduced

scenarios.name: Documentation excluded
scenarios.then: the docs/ directory is not sent to the build daemon
and_then: documentation files do not appear in any build layer

scenarios.name: Test files excluded
scenarios.then: files matching *_test.go and test scripts are not sent to the build daemon
and_then: test infrastructure does not bloat the build context

requirements.description: The Dockerfile SHALL pass hadolint linting with no errors and follow Dockerfile best practices
requirements.rationale: Hadolint catches common Dockerfile antipatterns: missing version pins, unnecessary layers, shell form vs exec form, etc.

scenarios.name: Hadolint passes with no errors
scenarios.when: hadolint is run against the Dockerfile
scenarios.then: no errors are reported
and_then: warnings may be present but are documented with inline ignores if necessary

scenarios.name: ENTRYPOINT uses exec form
scenarios.then: ENTRYPOINT uses JSON array syntax ["..."]
and_then: signals are properly forwarded to the plexd process

scenarios.name: Base images use version tags not latest
scenarios.then: all FROM statements use specific version tags (e.g., golang:1.24-alpine, not golang:latest)
and_then: builds are reproducible

requirements.description: The Dockerfile SHOULD support multi-platform builds for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 via TARGETPLATFORM build args
requirements.rationale: plexd supports both amd64 and arm64 architectures. Docker buildx can produce multi-arch images using TARGETOS/TARGETARCH.

scenarios.name: Default platform builds successfully
scenarios.when: docker build is run without --platform flag
scenarios.then: the image is built for the host platform
and_then: GOARCH defaults to the host architecture

scenarios.name: Cross-platform build for arm64
scenarios.when: docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 is run on an amd64 host
scenarios.then: the image is built with GOARCH=arm64
and_then: the resulting binary is an arm64 ELF executable

scenarios.name: TARGETOS and TARGETARCH are used in go build
scenarios.then: the go build command uses GOOS=$TARGETOS GOARCH=$TARGETARCH
and_then: Docker automatically sets these args during multi-platform builds

requirements.description: The .dockerignore file SHALL be placed at the repository root to apply to all Docker builds
requirements.rationale: Docker uses .dockerignore from the build context root (repo root). A .dockerignore inside deploy/docker/ would not apply when building from the repo root.

scenarios.name: .dockerignore applies to docker build from repo root
scenarios.when: running docker build -f deploy/docker/Dockerfile . from the repo root
scenarios.then: the .dockerignore at the repo root filters the build context
and_then: .git, docs, and test files are excluded

scenarios.name: .dockerignore does not exclude required build files
scenarios.then: go.mod, go.sum, cmd/, internal/, Makefile are included in the build context
and_then: the build has all necessary source files

scenarios.name: Deploy files are excluded except the Dockerfile itself
scenarios.then: deploy/systemd, deploy/kubernetes, deploy/cloud-init are excluded
and_then: only source code needed for compilation is in the context

review_criteria: Multi-stage Dockerfile builds successfully with `docker build -f deploy/docker/Dockerfile .` from repo root and produces a working plexd image
Binary is statically compiled (CGO_ENABLED=0) and runs on distroless/static-debian12 base without runtime errors
Build args VERSION, COMMIT, DATE are correctly wired to main.go ldflags (main.version, main.commit, main.date)
Module cache optimization: go.mod/go.sum copied and `go mod download` run before full source COPY
Container runs as non-root user (UID 65534) with /var/lib/plexd, /var/run/plexd, /etc/plexd directories pre-created
Ports 9100/tcp and 51820/udp are exposed; entrypoint is exec-form ["/usr/local/bin/plexd"]
hadolint reports no errors on the Dockerfile; base images use specific version tags, not :latest
.dockerignore at repo root excludes .git, docs, test files, and deploy subdirectories (systemd, kubernetes, cloud-init)
Multi-platform support via TARGETOS/TARGETARCH args enables buildx cross-compilation for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64
Reference documentation in docs/reference/backend/dockerfile.md covers build commands, args, ports, and runtime user
implementation_notes:
This is a pure infrastructure task — no Go code changes required. The Dockerfile follows the standard multi-stage Go build pattern.

**Architecture decisions:**
- **Base images:** golang:1.24-alpine for builder (matches go.mod 1.24.0), gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12 for runtime (no shell, minimal attack surface, includes CA certs)
- **Static compilation:** CGO_ENABLED=0 produces a fully static binary that runs on distroless without libc
- **ldflags:** -s -w strips debug info and DWARF tables to reduce binary size. -X injects version/commit/date matching cmd/plexd/main.go vars
- **Module cache:** COPY go.mod go.sum → go mod download → COPY . . is the standard Docker cache optimization for Go
- **User:** UID 65534 (nobody) is the standard non-root user in distroless images
- **Ports:** 9100 matches daemonset.yaml healthz/readyz probes and README node_api.http.listen default. 51820 matches README wireguard.listen_port default
- **.dockerignore placement:** Must be at repo root because Docker reads it from the build context root. The feature description says deploy/docker/.dockerignore but Docker build context is the repo root, so the file goes at .dockerignore in the repo root
- **Multi-platform:** Using Docker's automatic TARGETOS/TARGETARCH args with ARG declarations in the builder stage

**Key files to reference:**
- cmd/plexd/main.go — ldflags vars (version, commit, date)
- deploy/kubernetes/daemonset.yaml — port 9100 probes, security context, volume mounts, resource limits
- go.mod — Go 1.24.0 version
- .github/workflows/ci.yml — existing CI pattern (Go 1.24)
- Makefile — add docker-build target alongside existing build/test/lint

**Pitfalls:**
- .dockerignore at deploy/docker/.dockerignore would NOT work — Docker reads .dockerignore from the build context root
- go.sum must be copied alongside go.mod for `go mod download` to work
- TARGETOS/TARGETARCH must be declared as ARG after FROM to be available in the build stage
- distroless has no shell — cannot use RUN mkdir in runtime stage, must use COPY --from or multi-stage techniques for directory creation
